claims.text: Stable sustained VT: IV amiodarone is often used but works slowly
claims.quote: IV amiodarone is frequently used but does not usually work quickly.

claims.text: (if lidocaine is ineffective, IV procainamide may be given but may take up to 1 hour); if they fail, cardiovert.
claims.quote: If lidocaine is ineffective, IV procainamide may be given, but it may take up to 1 hour to work. IV amiodarone is frequently used but does not usually work quickly. Failure of IV procainamide or IV amiodarone is an indication for cardioversion.

claims.text: Long-term: after sustained VT with no transient or reversible cause, patients typically require an ICD; if an ICD can't be used, amiodarone may be preferred;
claims.quote: In the absence of a transient or reversible cause, patients who have had an episode of sustained VT typically require an ICD (1). Most patients with sustained VT and a significant structural heart disorder should also receive a beta-blocker. If an ICD cannot be used, amiodarone may be the preferred antiarrhythmic for prevention of sudden death.

claims.text: to prevent recurrences BB first, then sotalol, then amiodarone.
claims.quote: Because beta-blockers (class II) are safe, they are the first choice unless contraindicated. If an additional medication is required, sotalol is commonly used, then amiodarone (1).

claims.text: Oral amiodarone (recurrent VF/unstable VT): load 800–1600 mg/day for 1–3 weeks, then 600–800 mg/day for 1 month, then usually 400 mg/day;
claims.quote: Initiate treatment with a loading dose of 800 to 1600 mg/day until initial therapeutic response occurs (usually 1 to 3 weeks). Once adequate arrhythmia control is achieved, or if side effects become prominent, reduce Pacerone tablet dose to 600 to 800 mg/day for one month and then to the maintenance dose, usually 400 mg/day.

claims.quote: Correct hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, and hypocalcemia before initiating treatment.

claims.text: Interactions (persist weeks–months after stopping):
claims.quote: Because of amiodarone's long half-life, expect drug interactions to persist for weeks to months after discontinuation of amiodarone.

claims.text: warfarin—PT rises ~100% in 3–4 days, cut warfarin by ⅓–½;
claims.quote: Coadministration increases prothrombin time by 100% after 3 to 4 days. Reduce warfarin dose by one-third to one-half and monitor prothrombin times.

claims.text: digoxin—halve the dose or stop;
claims.quote: Reduce digoxin by half or discontinue.

claims.text: simvastatin ≤20 mg;
claims.quote: Limit the coadministered dose of simvastatin to 20 mg.

claims.text: other QT-prolonging drugs—avoid (torsades);
claims.quote: | Increased risk of Torsade de Pointes. Avoid concomitant use.

claims.text: sofosbuvir—symptomatic bradycardia.
claims.quote: Cases of symptomatic bradyarrhythmia requiring pacemaker insertion have been reported in patients on oral maintenance amiodarone who initiated therapy with sofosbuvir.

claims.text: Amiodarone CI: cardiogenic shock;
claims.quote: Cardiogenic shock.

claims.text: sick sinus syndrome, second- or third-degree AV block or bradycardia with syncope without a pacemaker;
claims.quote: Sick sinus syndrome, second- or third-degree atrioventricular block, bradycardia leading to syncope without a functioning pacemaker.

claims.text: iodine hypersensitivity.
claims.quote: Known hypersensitivity to the drug or to any of its components, including iodine.

claims.text: Counsel: photosensitivity in about 10%; use sunscreen or protective clothing.
claims.quote: Pacerone induces photosensitization in about 10% of patients; some protection may be afforded sun-barrier creams or protective clothing.

claims.text: Overdose: monitor rhythm and BP; β-agonist or pacemaker for bradycardia;
claims.quote: Monitor the patient's cardiac rhythm and blood pressure, and, if bradycardia ensues, a β-adrenergic agonist or a pacemaker may be used.

claims.text: inotropes/vasopressors for hypotension;
claims.quote: Treat hypotension with inadequate tissue perfusion with positive inotropic and vasopressor agents.

claims.text: not dialyzable.
claims.quote: Neither Pacerone nor its metabolite is dialyzable.
